Current question: How does Font::memory_face choose a format and create a usable face? Start with its ordered dispatch and invalid input or face-index branches. Then explain which SFNT tables are required, how missing tables differ from malformed table contents, and where errors propagate. Show the real code paths and useful diagrams.

sections.title: Format dispatch and fall-through
sections.prose: Font::memory_face gives earlier probes priority: a PCF_FILE_VERSION match calls pcf_face, otherwise a PFR0 prefix calls pfr_face, otherwise a 0x0200 or 0x0300 header calls winfnt_face. Each matching branch returns immediately, so later format checks do not run. Next, memory_face treats text as BDF only when its first BDF keyword passes is_bdf_probe_keyword; a parse_bdf_constructor_error is returned immediately, while no preflight error proceeds to bdf_face. After BDF, the ordered probes are a Resource-CIDFont prefix to cid_type1_face, recognizable data from type42_sfnt_data to type42_face, and type1_cleartext to type1_face; each matching probe returns its constructor result. If at least 17 bytes are all control bytes, memory_face returns InvalidFileFormat before trying truetype_face. Otherwise truetype_face runs first; on its error, inputs at least 118 bytes get a winfnt_face attempt, whose success wins, whose UnknownFileFormat wins only when has_winfnt_header_shape is true, and whose other errors leave the original TrueType error in place; shorter inputs return that original error directly.
